Occupational English Test

WRITING SUB-TEST: MEDICINE
SAMPLE RESPONSE: LETTER




Dr Mary Bellamy
Plastic Surgery Consultant
Shepton Hospital
Shepton




                  l
21 May 2019




              n ra
Dear Dr Bellamy



            io e
Re: Mr Richard McKie
          ut en
DOB: 26.05.1998

I am writing to you concerning further management of Mr Richard McKie, a fourth-year medical student, who was
involved today in a motorcycle accident in which he sustained a right blowout fracture, a LeFort type II fracture and
       rib g

right tension pneumothorax; the latter is now resolved.

On admission, Mr McKie was experiencing respiratory distress, was diaphoretic and cyanotic; pulse-oximetry was
     st or


88%. He was stabilised with the insertion of a right chest tube and oxygen. The thorax X-ray showed 5th rib midline
facture, with no hemothorax. Two litres of oxygen were given via nasal cannula. Medications include: hydromorphone
0.5 mg IV 4-hourly; ampicillin-sulbactam 1g IV 6-hourly; omeprazole 40 mg IV once daily and enoxaparin 40 mg
   di t f



subcutaneously once daily.

Upon a secondary survey, the following presented: right periorbital ecchymosis and edema with reduced visual acuity
        o




and mild enophthalmos and diplopia (especially in the upgaze). A head CT scan revealed a blowout fracture with
inferior rectus entrapment, and LeFort type ll fracture.
      N




Mr McKie now shows normal vital signs, no respiratory distress, and is haemodynamically stable with the chest tube
in position. I am therefore referring him to you for management of his blowout fracture with plastic or maxillofacial
surgery.

Please contact me if you need further information.

Yours sincerely




Doctor
